raw_results.title: AbortSignal cancel fetch request safely
raw_results.snippet: AbortSignal lets an application cancel a fetch request through an AbortController. The caller passes the signal to fetch and aborts the controller when work is no longer needed. This long synthetic passage exercises the shared evidence budget while retaining the source URL and provider-family signals.

raw_results.title: Cancel a fetch request with AbortController
raw_results.snippet: Create an AbortController, pass controller.signal to the fetch request, and call controller.abort to cancel pending work. The rejected request should be handled as an expected cancellation path. This synthetic result is intentionally verbose so progressive disclosure is observable without live content.

raw_results.title: Abort signal composition for request cancellation
raw_results.snippet: Request cancellation can combine an explicit abort signal with a bounded timeout. Consumers should forward the same cancellation signal through rate limiting, retries, HTTP requests, and enrichment. This synthetic result provides a second independent route through the evidence basket.

raw_results.title: Handle aborted fetch operations
raw_results.snippet: Applications distinguish an intentional aborted fetch operation from other network failures and preserve enough context for callers to decide whether work should continue. The result remains a compact source reference after the full-result budget is exhausted.

raw_results.title: Forward cancellation across async boundaries
raw_results.snippet: Forwarding one AbortSignal across asynchronous boundaries prevents work from surviving after its caller has cancelled the operation. The example is synthetic and exists only to demonstrate the bounded evidence response contract.
